item.text:
**Verdict:** **Yes, strongly**. In 2024 AMLO articulated a very clear governing program: the 4T / *humanismo mexicano*, “first the poor,” anti-neoliberal redistribution, sovereignty, direct welfare delivery, and anti-corruption. The caveat is that the same program also revealed a power-consolidation track, especially around courts, electoral institutions, and information controls.

## Accepted Claims

### Positive / program clarity
- [Me dediqué a servir al pueblo: presidente AMLO](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/prensa/me-dedique-a-servir-al-pueblo-presidente-amlo?idiom=es) | Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 | 2024-09-30 | Claim: AMLO explicitly framed his rule as “first the poor,” anti-corruption, and service to the people, presenting the 4T as a coherent governing model rather than a loose campaign style. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Bienestar, salud, obras y basificación a personal educativo y médico, prioridades en último tramo de la 4T: presidente](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/bienestar-salud-obras-y-basificacion-a-personal-educativo-y-medico-prioridades-en-ultimo-tramo-de-la-4t-presidente/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-01-02 | Claim: He set a concrete end-of-term agenda: universal health care, welfare programs, completed public works, and permanent staffing for teachers and health workers. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Paquete de iniciativas de reforma del Gobierno de México significa la llegada del humanismo mexicano a la Constitución](https://www.gob.mx/segob/prensa/paquete-de-iniciativas-de-reforma-del-gobierno-de-mexico-significa-la-llegada-del-humanismo-mexicano-a-la-constitucion) | Secretaría de Gobernación | 2024-02-05 | Claim: The government said its February reform package would constitutionalize “humanismo mexicano” as a new social pact protecting the most vulnerable. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Cuarta Transformación acabó con subordinación de México a extranjeros: presidente](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/cuarta-transformacion-acabo-con-subordinacion-de-mexico-a-extranjeros-presidente/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-05-05 | Claim: AMLO tied the 4T to sovereignty, anti-neoliberalism, anti-corruption, and independence from foreign pressure, giving the program a clear strategic-national frame. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Trabajadores del Poder Judicial están en su derecho de manifestarse: presidente; reforma constitucional no les perjudica, reitera](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/trabajadores-del-poder-judicial-estan-en-su-derecho-de-manifestarse-presidente-reforma-constitucional-no-les-perjudica-reitera/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-08-19 | Claim: He said the judicial reform was meant to end corruption and privileges, especially among top judges, so the reform was presented as a corrective governance program. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Versión estenográfica. 25-06-24](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/25-06-24-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-06-25 | Claim: AMLO said he would not seek reelection and would leave office, a concrete anti-personalist commitment later matched by the transition. | Question IDs: 8B.1

### Negative / revealed power goals
- [Mexico constitutional reforms more likely with super-majority in sight](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexico-constitutional-reforms-more-likely-with-supermajority-in-sight-3469906) | Reuters | 2024-06-04 | Claim: Reuters reported AMLO’s reform push would scrap or weaken independent oversight bodies and overhaul the INE; critics said the plan would cement Morena hegemony, revealing a regime-control goal alongside policy aims. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Mexico's sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588) | Reuters | 2024-09-15 | Claim: The reform was publicly justified as serving ordinary citizens, but critics said it would end judicial independence and concentrate power in the executive. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Mexico](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: The overview says AMLO’s final year featured repeated attacks on journalists and the NYT phone-number episode, suggesting narrative control and intimidation alongside the formal ideology. | Question IDs: 8B.1
- [Mexico country chapter](https://www.hrw.org/es/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | Claim: HRW said AMLO and his party blocked INAI appointments, leaving the transparency body unable to function normally and weakening the oversight infrastructure that would test and constrain the program. | Question IDs: 8B.1

## Synthesis

AMLO’s 2024 ideology is not hard to identify. He repeatedly defined it as *humanismo mexicano*, anti-neoliberal redistribution, sovereignty, and “first the poor,” then translated that into welfare expansion, health/public-works priorities, and constitutional reform language. That is a clear governing program.

The caveat is that the program also had a revealed institutional strategy: weaken or bypass independent checks, especially the INE, INAI, and the judiciary. So for 8B.1, the answer is **yes, clearly articulated**, but the content of the program includes **both policy direction and regime-control goals**.

## Search Gap

I did not find one independent 2024 document that cleanly maps the whole ideology and then measures later action against it. The strongest evidence is distributed across official speeches/self-descriptions and a smaller set of Reuters / HRW / Reuters Institute reports. That makes the program very clear, but the “later action” test is only partially independent because many positive claims are government self-portraits.
